results.name: set_level_yes_rate_dispersion
results.description: Standard deviation across sets (with >=30 responses) of each set's overall yes rate; observed > null means sets differ in how broadly people generalise more than the model's features capture (model too homogeneous across sets), observed < null the reverse.

results.name: factor_rule_example_count_gain
results.description: Among multi-example sets with common factor gcd>=3, yes rate on targets that are multiples of the gcd for sets of 3-4 examples minus for sets of 2 examples; observed > null means more examples strengthen the factor rule (size principle) more than the model's constant factor boost predicts.
results.code:
# name: factor_rule_example_count_gain
# description: Among multi-example sets with common factor gcd>=3, yes rate on targets that are multiples of the gcd for sets of 3-4 examples minus for sets of 2 examples; observed > null means more examples strengthen the factor rule (size principle) more than the model's constant factor boost predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    import math
    from functools import reduce
    sets = df["number_set"].unique()
    g = {s: reduce(math.gcd, [int(x) for x in s.split(",")]) for s in sets}
    gg = df["number_set"].map(g).values
    n = (df["number_set"].str.count(",") + 1).values
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].values.astype(float)
    mult = (gg >= 3) & (t % np.maximum(gg, 1) == 0)
    a = mult & (n >= 3)
    b = mult & (n == 2)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: round_factor_tens_vs_fives
results.description: Among sets whose examples' gcd is exactly 5 (e.g. 5; 5,65; 90,100,5), yes rate on targets that are multiples of 10 minus yes rate on odd multiples of 5 (both are multiples of the common factor, which the model credits equally); observed > null means people favour round tens over fives beyond what the model predicts.
results.code:
# name: round_factor_tens_vs_fives
# description: Among sets whose examples' gcd is exactly 5 (e.g. 5; 5,65; 90,100,5), yes rate on targets that are multiples of 10 minus yes rate on odd multiples of 5 (both are multiples of the common factor, which the model credits equally); observed > null means people favour round tens over fives beyond what the model predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    import math
    from functools import reduce
    sets = df["number_set"].unique()
    g = {s: reduce(math.gcd, [int(x) for x in s.split(",")]) for s in sets}
    gg = df["number_set"].map(g).values
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].values.astype(float)
    m = gg == 5
    a = m & (t % 10 == 0)
    b = m & (t % 5 == 0) & (t % 10 != 0)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: small_set_low_target_preference
results.description: Among sets whose examples are all <=10, for targets that are not multiples of a gcd>=3, yes rate on targets 11-30 minus yes rate on targets 51-100; observed > null means people favour nearby-but-outside small targets over far large ones more than the model's decade-band familiarity predicts, observed < null the reverse.
results.code:
# name: small_set_low_target_preference
# description: Among sets whose examples are all <=10, for targets that are not multiples of a gcd>=3, yes rate on targets 11-30 minus yes rate on targets 51-100; observed > null means people favour nearby-but-outside small targets over far large ones more than the model's decade-band familiarity predicts, observed < null the reverse.
def test_statistic(df):
    import math
    from functools import reduce
    sets = df["number_set"].unique()
    rows = {s: (reduce(math.gcd, [int(x) for x in s.split(",")]), max(int(x) for x in s.split(","))) for s in sets}
    ns = df["number_set"]
    gg = ns.map({k: v[0] for k, v in rows.items()}).values
    mx = ns.map({k: v[1] for k, v in rows.items()}).values
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].values.astype(float)
    mult = (gg >= 3) & (t % np.maximum(gg, 1) == 0)
    base = (mx <= 10) & ~mult
    a = base & (t >= 11) & (t <= 30)
    b = base & (t >= 51)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: factor_multiple_inside_vs_outside_range
results.description: Among multi-example sets with gcd>=3, for targets that are multiples of the gcd, yes rate when the target lies within [min,max] of the examples minus when it lies outside; observed > null means people restrict the factor rule to the examples' range more than the model (which pre-empts magnitude under a rule) predicts, observed < null the reverse.
results.code:
# name: factor_multiple_inside_vs_outside_range
# description: Among multi-example sets with gcd>=3, for targets that are multiples of the gcd, yes rate when the target lies within [min,max] of the examples minus when it lies outside; observed > null means people restrict the factor rule to the examples' range more than the model (which pre-empts magnitude under a rule) predicts, observed < null the reverse.
def test_statistic(df):
    import math
    from functools import reduce
    sets = df["number_set"].unique()
    info = {}
    for s in sets:
        xs = [int(x) for x in s.split(",")]
        info[s] = (reduce(math.gcd, xs), min(xs), max(xs), len(xs))
    gg = df["number_set"].map({k: v[0] for k, v in info.items()}).values
    lo = df["number_set"].map({k: v[1] for k, v in info.items()}).values
    hi = df["number_set"].map({k: v[2] for k, v in info.items()}).values
    n = df["number_set"].map({k: v[3] for k, v in info.items()}).values
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].values.astype(float)
    mult = (n >= 2) & (gg >= 3) & (t % np.maximum(gg, 1) == 0)
    inside = (t >= lo) & (t <= hi)
    a = mult & inside
    b = mult & ~inside
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: shared_decade_within_band
results.description: Among multi-example sets with no explicit rule (gcd<3 and not all same final digit), for targets inside the examples' decade band that share no final digit with any example, yes rate when the target shares a tens digit with some example minus when it does not; observed > null means people use specific-decade similarity that the model's flat within-band familiarity misses.
results.code:
# name: shared_decade_within_band
# description: Among multi-example sets with no explicit rule (gcd<3 and not all same final digit), for targets inside the examples' decade band that share no final digit with any example, yes rate when the target shares a tens digit with some example minus when it does not; observed > null means people use specific-decade similarity that the model's flat within-band familiarity misses.
def test_statistic(df):
    import math
    from functools import reduce
    sets = df["number_set"].unique()
    rows = {}
    for s in sets:
        xs = [int(x) for x in s.split(",")]
        g = reduce(math.gcd, xs)
        uni = len({x % 10 for x in xs}) == 1
        rule = len(xs) >= 2 and (g >= 3 or uni)
        dec = 0
        dig = 0
        for x in xs:
            dec |= 1 << (x // 10)
            dig |= 1 << (x % 10)
        rows[s] = (len(xs) >= 2 and not rule, min(x // 10 for x in xs), max(x // 10 for x in xs), dec, dig)
    ns = df["number_set"]
    ok = ns.map({k: v[0] for k, v in rows.items()}).values.astype(bool)
    lo = ns.map({k: v[1] for k, v in rows.items()}).values
    hi = ns.map({k: v[2] for k, v in rows.items()}).values
    dec = ns.map({k: v[3] for k, v in rows.items()}).values.astype(np.int64)
    dig = ns.map({k: v[4] for k, v in rows.items()}).values.astype(np.int64)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].values.astype(float)
    td = t // 10
    share_dec = ((dec >> td) & 1) == 1
    share_dig = ((dig >> (t % 10)) & 1) == 1
    base = ok & (td >= lo) & (td <= hi) & ~share_dig
    a = base & share_dec
    b = base & ~share_dec
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: rule_discrimination_late_minus_early
results.description: For multi-example rule sets (gcd>=3 or all examples share a final digit), the rule-consistent minus rule-inconsistent yes-rate gap in late trials (trial_index above median) minus that gap in early trials; observed > null means people become more rule-bound over the session (observed < null: less), a change the stationary model cannot produce.
results.code:
# name: rule_discrimination_late_minus_early
# description: For multi-example rule sets (gcd>=3 or all examples share a final digit), the rule-consistent minus rule-inconsistent yes-rate gap in late trials (trial_index above median) minus that gap in early trials; observed > null means people become more rule-bound over the session (observed < null: less), a change the stationary model cannot produce.
def test_statistic(df):
    import math
    from functools import reduce
    sets = df["number_set"].unique()
    rows = {}
    for s in sets:
        xs = [int(x) for x in s.split(",")]
        g = reduce(math.gcd, xs)
        uni = len({x % 10 for x in xs}) == 1
        rows[s] = (len(xs) >= 2 and (g >= 3 or uni), g, xs[0] % 10 if uni else -1)
    ns = df["number_set"]
    isrule = ns.map({k: v[0] for k, v in rows.items()}).values.astype(bool)
    gg = ns.map({k: v[1] for k, v in rows.items()}).values
    ud = ns.map({k: v[2] for k, v in rows.items()}).values
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].values.astype(float)
    ti = df["trial_index"].values
    cons = ((gg >= 3) & (t % np.maximum(gg, 1) == 0)) | (t % 10 == ud)
    late = ti > np.median(ti)
    out = []
    for half in (late, ~late):
        a = isrule & half & cons
        b = isrule & half & ~cons
        if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
            return 0.0
        out.append(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())
    return float(out[0] - out[1])

results.name: above_vs_below_range_asymmetry
results.description: Among all sets, for targets sharing no final digit with any example and not multiples of a gcd>=3, yes rate for targets above the largest example minus targets below the smallest example; observed > null means people generalise upward more than the model's symmetric decade-band familiarity predicts (observed < null: downward).
results.code:
# name: above_vs_below_range_asymmetry
# description: Among all sets, for targets sharing no final digit with any example and not multiples of a gcd>=3, yes rate for targets above the largest example minus targets below the smallest example; observed > null means people generalise upward more than the model's symmetric decade-band familiarity predicts (observed < null: downward).
def test_statistic(df):
    import math
    from functools import reduce
    sets = df["number_set"].unique()
    rows = {}
    for s in sets:
        xs = [int(x) for x in s.split(",")]
        dig = 0
        for x in xs:
            dig |= 1 << (x % 10)
        rows[s] = (reduce(math.gcd, xs), min(xs), max(xs), dig)
    ns = df["number_set"]
    gg = ns.map({k: v[0] for k, v in rows.items()}).values
    lo = ns.map({k: v[1] for k, v in rows.items()}).values
    hi = ns.map({k: v[2] for k, v in rows.items()}).values
    dig = ns.map({k: v[3] for k, v in rows.items()}).values.astype(np.int64)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].values.astype(float)
    mult = (gg >= 3) & (t % np.maximum(gg, 1) == 0)
    share_dig = ((dig >> (t % 10)) & 1) == 1
    base = ~mult & ~share_dig
    a = base & (t > hi)
    b = base & (t < lo)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())
